summary: Depth-first rabbithole dossier for $unionWith; source-anchored research pack.

facts.text: **C4 — Two syntaxes exist; the short form `{ $unionWith: "<coll>" }` means "all documents, unprocessed".** The full form is `{ $unionWith: { coll: "<collection>", pipeline: [ ... ] } }`. `coll` may name a collection *or a view*.

4. The disallowed-usage set encoded in SERVER-45529 at implementation time was: `$unionWith` may not read from a sharded collection when it sits inside the inner pipeline of a `$lookup`; it may not be used in update pipelines; it is incompatible with `$changeStream`; and its sub-pipeline may not contain write stages, `$changeStream`, or stages that must run on `mongos`/the local host (`$listCachedAndActiveUsers`, `$listLocalSessions`, `$currentOp` with `localOps: true`, and internal change-stream stages). — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-45529

16. **MongoDB 6.0** — the `$unionWith` sub-pipeline may contain the Atlas Search / MongoDB Search `$search` or `$searchMeta` stage, and that stage must be **first** inside the sub-pipeline. This is the mechanism by which one query searches several collections in the same database, each with its own search index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.0/reference/operator/aggregation/unionwith.md — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/unionwith/

This report covers only the `$unionWith` stage itself: its parts (`coll`, `pipeline`), its execution mechanism inside the aggregation runtime, the invariants it guarantees and does not guarantee, and its documented limits. It does not cover sibling stages (`$lookup`, `$merge`, `$out`, `$documents`, `$facet`) except where they appear in a `$unionWith` restriction, and it does not cover the aggregation framework generally. Version statements are pinned to the MongoDB server release named in the source.

13. From 4.4 onward the sub-pipeline may not contain `$out` or `$merge`. This restriction has never been relaxed and is still listed in the current manual. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v4.4/reference/operator/aggregation/unionWith.md — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/unionwith/

1. **Exact version that dropped the sharded-collection restriction (claim 17).** Verified present in 5.0 and absent in 7.0. The v6.0 and v5.1 pages were not fetched, so the cut-over is bounded to 5.1–7.0 but not pinned. Claim 18 offers a mechanism (the 5.1 `$lookup` change) but no release note was found that names `$unionWith`.

**C6 — Since MongoDB 6.0, `$search` and `$searchMeta` may appear inside the `$unionWith` sub-pipeline, and must be its first stage.** This is the sanctioned mechanism for a single full-text query spanning several collections on an Atlas cluster. Each collection still needs its own search index, and the stage ordering constraint is hard: `$search` first or the operation errors. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/unionWith/ · https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-search/tutorial/cross-collection-tutorials/

**C10.** Collation resolution is asymmetric and surprising. If `aggregate()` specifies a `collation`, it wins and all others are ignored. If it does not: when `coll` is a **collection**, that collection's own collation is **ignored**; when `coll` is a **view**, its collation *"must match that of the top-level collection/view. Otherwise, the operation errors."* So the same pipeline is silently reinterpreted against a collection but hard-fails against a view. → https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/unionWith/

**C1.** An aggregation pipeline cannot use `$unionWith` inside a multi-document transaction. The restriction is still present in the current manual and was present in v7.0 — it has not been relaxed the way the `$lookup`-in-transaction restriction was in 8.0. → https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/unionWith/ → https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v7.0/reference/operator/aggregation/unionWith/
**C2.** The `$unionWith` sub-pipeline cannot include `$out`. → https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/unionWith/
**C3.** The `$unionWith` sub-pipeline cannot include `$merge`. → https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/unionWith/

**C4.** The `$unionWith` sub-pipeline cannot contain `$changeStream` or *any collection-less aggregation stage*, and cannot contain a stage that must run on `mongos` or the receiving host (`$listLocalSessions`, `$listCachedAndActiveUsers`, `$currentOp` with `localOps: true`, internal change-stream stages). This enumeration exists in the implementing ticket, not in the manual's Restrictions table. → https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-45529

**C6.** `$unionWith` cannot read from a **sharded** collection when it appears in the inner pipeline of a `$lookup`. Verbatim from the ticket: *"$unionWith is not allowed to read from a sharded collection if it is part of the inner pipeline of a $lookup."* Resolved into 4.3.4, 2020-02-06. → https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-45529

**C12.** `$unionWith` is **not** in the list of stages disallowed inside `$facet` (`$collStats`, `$facet`, `$geoNear`, `$indexStats`, `$out`, `$merge`, `$planCacheStats`, `$search`, `$searchMeta`, `$vectorSearch`). It is therefore legal inside a facet sub-pipeline — but because `$search` *is* on that list, the `$search`-inside-`$unionWith` pattern (C15) cannot be nested inside `$facet`. → https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/facet/

**C13.** **Breaking change in MongoDB 8.0.** Namespaces in subpipelines within `$lookup` and `$unionWith` are now validated for correct use of the `from`/`coll` fields. Supplying `coll` alongside a `$documents`-led sub-pipeline errors in 8.0+; *"In MongoDB versions before 8.0, the previous example runs."* This is a silent-to-loud upgrade hazard: pipelines that were merely redundant before 8.0 now fail. → https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/unionWith/

**C16.** `$$SEARCH_META` *"can be used anywhere after a `$search` stage in any pipeline, but it can't be used after the `$lookup` or `$unionWith` stage in any pipeline."* Combining a union with search metadata is therefore structurally impossible in one pipeline. → https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-search/aggregation-stages/search/

**C17.** `$unionWith` requires a 4.4.0+ server binary. Reports of `Unrecognized pipeline stage name: '$unionWith'` in 2022 traced to a stale test binary (`mongodb-memory-server` pinned below 4.4), not to a driver or production-server version — a failure mode that appears only in CI. → https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/unrecognized-pipeline-stage-name-unionwith/155602

**C18.** **Wrong results.** `DocumentSourceUnionWith::getDependencies()` was unimplemented, so it *"fail[ed] to report any of the variable references inside its sub-pipeline."* A `$unionWith` nested in a `$lookup` whose sub-pipeline referenced a correlated `let` variable was misclassified as non-correlated, materialized once, and produced *"incorrect query results."* Reported against 4.4.12, 5.0.5, 5.2.0-rc6; closed as a duplicate. → https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-63030

**C25.** `$unionWith` is **not** among the stages the manual lists as able to spill to disk under the 100 MB per-stage limit (`$bucket`, `$bucketAuto`, `$group`, `$setWindowFields`, `$sort` when not index-supported, `$sortByCount`). The limit therefore bites on the `$group`/`$sort` you add *after* a union, not on the union itself; combined with C24, deduplicating a large union is the realistic point of failure. → https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-limits/

**D3. A widely-circulated claim about 8.0 is a misreading.** Several secondary summaries state that "starting in MongoDB 8.0, an invalid `coll` field returns an error," and extrapolate that `$unionWith` against a **nonexistent collection** now errors. The manual's 8.0 example shows something narrower: the error arises because `coll: "cakeFlavors"` is supplied *alongside* a `$documents`-led sub-pipeline — a namespace-validation error about field combination, not about collection existence. Do not assume 8.0 changed missing-collection behavior on the basis of that sentence. → https://www.mongodb

The MongoDB 4.4 release notes state verbatim: *"MongoDB 4.4 adds the `$unionWith` aggregation stage, providing the ability to combines pipeline results from multiple collections into a single result set."* (The grammatical error is in the source.) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v4.4/release-notes/4.4.md

From 4.4 onward, *"An aggregation pipeline cannot use `$unionWith` inside transactions."* The restriction is listed identically in the 4.4, 5.0, 7.0, 8.0 and current manuals. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v4.4/reference/operator/aggregation/unionWith.md — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/unionwith/

The transaction restriction is enforced at runtime with the error string **`Stage not supported inside of a multi-document transaction: $unionWith`**, reported by a user on the MongoDB Community forum on **2023-11-01** while attempting foreign-key validation inside a multi-document transaction. — https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/stage-not-supported-inside-of-a-multi-document-transaction-unionwith/251779

17. **The sharded-collection restriction was dropped between 5.0 and 7.0.** The 4.4 and 5.0 manuals both carry a "Sharded Collection" restriction row — *"If the `$unionWith` stage is part of the `$lookup` pipeline, the `$unionWith` `coll` cannot be sharded"* — plus a worked `inventory_q1` example. The v7.0, v8.0 and current manuals list only three restrictions (transactions, `$out`, `$merge`); the sharded row and its example are gone. — present: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v4.4/reference/operator/aggregation/unionWith.md — present: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v5.0/reference/operator/aggregat

18. The most likely cause of claim 17 is the **MongoDB 5.1** change that allowed sharded collections in the `from` parameter of `$lookup`: *"Starting in MongoDB 5.1, you can specify sharded collections in the `from` parameter of `$lookup` stages."* Because the dropped `$unionWith` restriction existed only for `$unionWith` nested inside a `$lookup` sub-pipeline, removing the `$lookup` sharding limitation removes its premise. This is an inference from two official pages, not a statement found in a release note. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/lookup.md

21. **MongoDB 8.0 is a breaking change**, flagged on the page as "Changed in version 8.0": namespaces in `$lookup` and `$unionWith` sub-pipelines are now validated. If the sub-pipeline starts with a stage that needs no collection (`$documents`), `coll` must be omitted; if it starts with a stage that needs one (`$match`, `$collStats`), `coll` must be present. The manual's own example — `db.cakeFlavors.aggregate([{ $unionWith: { coll: "cakeFlavors", pipeline: [ { $documents: [] } ] } }])` — *"returns an error"* in 8.0 and *"In MongoDB versions before 8.0, the previous example runs."* — https://w

- **Was the transaction ban lifted in 8.0?** Checked deliberately, because MongoDB 8.0 *did* relax a comparable limit for the sibling stage (*"Starting in MongoDB 8.0, you can use the `$lookup` stage within a transaction while targeting a sharded collection"*). No equivalent relaxation exists for `$unionWith`: the v8.0 and current manuals both still list the transaction restriction. Claim 14 survives. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/lookup.md — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.0/reference/operator/aggregation/unionwith.md

11. The stage is implemented by `DocumentSourceUnionWith` in `src/mongo/db/pipeline/document_source_union_with.{h,cpp}`. Its execution is a four-state machine, `ExecutionProgress`: `kIteratingSource` ("We haven't yet iterated 'pSource' to completion"), `kStartingSubPipeline` ("We finished iterating 'pSource', but haven't started on the sub pipeline and need to do some setup first"), `kIteratingSubPipeline`, and `kFinished`. <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/pipeline/document_source_union_with.h> 12. **C2 — De-duplication is a separate, explicit step: add a `$group` *after* the `$unionWith`.** The manual's worked example projects `state` from `suppliers` and `warehouses`, shows the duplicate `Colorado` in the output, then removes it with `{ $group: { _id: "$state" } }`. Percona's pre-release write-up flags the same point as the practical caveat: to get a `UNION DISTINCT` result "you must add a `$group` stage _after_ the `$unionWith` stage." Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v5.0/reference/operator/aggregation/unionWith.md · https://www.percona.com/blog/2020/06/11/mongodb-4-4-coming-out

**C7 — MongoDB 8.0 tightened namespace validation for `$unionWith` sub-pipelines.** The current manual is marked "Changed in version 8.0": namespaces in sub-pipelines within `$lookup` and `$unionWith` are validated for correct use of `from`/`coll`. Concretely, when the sub-pipeline begins with `$documents`, you must *omit* `coll`; including `coll` alongside `$documents` now returns an error where earlier versions tolerated it. This is a real upgrade-breaking change for pipelines that fabricated literal documents into a union.

**C8 — The `$unionWith` sub-pipeline cannot contain `$out` or `$merge`.** This has been in the restrictions table since 4.4 and remains in the current manual. The *outer* pipeline may still end in `$out`/`$merge`. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v7.0/reference/operator/aggregation/unionWith/ · https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/unionWith/

**C9 — An aggregation pipeline cannot use `$unionWith` inside a transaction.** Stated verbatim in the restrictions table of v5.0, v7.0, and the current manual. Operational consequence: a read that must be transactionally consistent with other reads/writes in the same session cannot use `$unionWith`; you must issue separate reads or accept non-transactional semantics. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v5.0/reference/operator/aggregation/unionWith.md · https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v7.0/reference/operator/aggregation/unionWith/

**C12 — `$unionWith` is *not* on the list of stages disallowed inside `$facet`.** The `$facet` "Behavior" section enumerates its exclusions — `$collStats`, `$facet`, `$geoNear`, `$indexStats`, `$out`, `$merge`, `$planCacheStats`, `$search`, `$searchMeta`, `$vectorSearch` — and `$unionWith` is absent. A multi-collection union may therefore appear inside a facet branch. (Note the interaction with C6: `$search` *is* excluded from `$facet`, so the `$search`-inside-`$unionWith` pattern cannot be nested inside a `$facet`.)

**C13 — Historically, a `$unionWith` nested inside a `$lookup` sub-pipeline could not target a sharded `coll`. That restriction row is present in the v5.0 manual and absent from the current manual.** The v5.0 page carries a dedicated section, "`$unionWith` a Sharded Collection": "If the `$unionWith` stage is part of the $lookup pipeline, the `$unionWith` `coll` cannot be sharded," with a worked example in which `inventory_q1` cannot be sharded. The corresponding row is gone from the v7.0 and current restriction tables. The most plausible reading is that the rule lapsed once `$lookup` gained sh

**Implication:** a pipeline written as `[...] , {$unionWith: "b"}, {$sort: {...}}, {$group: {...}}` materialises every document from both branches and then does a blocking, non-indexed sort/group over the union. Push the selective work *into* each branch by hand — `$match`, `$project`, `$limit`, and a per-branch `$group` inside the `$unionWith` `pipeline` — and do only the final merge outside. The engine will not do this rewrite for you. Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-48120 · https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-48121 · https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-45534

**C15 — Execution is lazy and source-first: the stage iterates its input source to exhaustion before it begins iterating the sub-pipeline, and a downstream `$limit` can prevent the sub-pipeline from ever running.** The server implementation initialises its shared state to `ExecutionProgress::kIteratingSource` and advances to `kIteratingSubPipeline`; the explain serialisation logic branches on "whether or not to explain the sub-pipeline depends on if we've started reading from it," and explicitly contemplates the case where "a `$limit` prevents sub-pipeline execution." 1. **Always assume duplicates.** If the downstream consumer needs distinct rows, add the `$group` yourself (C1, C2). There is no `UNION DISTINCT` keyword. 2. **Never rely on output order without an explicit `$sort`.** Order is documented as unspecified (C1). 3. **Do the selective work inside each branch.** `$match`, `$project`, `$limit`, and partial `$group` belong in the `$unionWith` `pipeline`, because the optimizer will not move them there (C14). 4. **Do not use `$unionWith` in a transaction.** It is a hard error; redesign the read or drop the transaction (C9). 5. **Check collation when eit

**C3 — Unlike SQL `UNION`, `$unionWith` imposes no schema-compatibility requirement on the two sides.** SQL `UNION` requires identical column counts and compatible types; `$unionWith` "doesn't impose these limitations," so collections with different shapes can be unioned directly. This is an operational advantage when unioning heterogeneous event or audit collections, and a correctness hazard when downstream stages assume a uniform shape. Source: https://database.guide/unionwith-mongodbs-equivalent-of-union-all/ (dated 2021-01-13)

**C5 — `$unionWith` was introduced in MongoDB 4.4 (GA 2020-07-30); sharded- collection support was implemented before release, in dev build 4.3.4.** SERVER-45526 "Support union with sharded collections" was created 2020-01-13 and resolved Fixed on 2020-02-03 with fix version 4.3.4 (the 4.4 development series). So, unlike `$lookup` — whose `from` collection could not be sharded until MongoDB 5.1 — `$unionWith` could target sharded collections from its first shipping release. Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-45526 · https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregatio

**Concept:** MongoDB aggregation stage `$unionWith` **Parent context:** mongodb-aggregation-stages-deep **Report date:** 2026-09-19 **Quality gate:** Met. 6 independent hosts consulted (`mongodb.com/docs`, `jira.mongodb.org`, `mongodb.com/community` forums, `mongodb.com/docs/drivers` compatibility pages, `educative.io`, `oneuptime.com`). Primary sources (official manual, official issue tracker) carry every load-bearing claim; secondary blog/forum sources are used only where flagged, and a disconfirming check against the docs is recorded in §4.

This report covers only the `$unionWith` aggregation stage: where it is disallowed, where it silently changes semantics, where the server has shipped incorrect results or unsafe memory behavior, and where documentation and practice disagree. It deliberately excludes `$lookup`, `$facet`, `$documents`, `$merge`, and `$out` except where their interaction with `$unionWith` is the edge case itself. Platform-compatibility claims are limited to whether `$unionWith` exists at all on a given engine.

**C5.** `$unionWith` is disallowed inside an update pipeline, and disallowed alongside a `$changeStream`. Same source as C4; again absent from the manual's Restrictions table. → https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-45529

**C7.** At the **top level** of a pipeline, `$unionWith` against a sharded collection is supported; sharded-collection support was implemented in 4.3.4 (pre-4.4 release train). → https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-45526

**C8.** `$unionWith` is `UNION ALL`, not `UNION`. *"The combined results from the previous stage and the `$unionWith` stage can include duplicates."* Deduplication requires an explicit `$group` after the union. → https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/unionWith/

**C11.** `_id` collisions across the two branches are not detected or resolved — `$unionWith` performs no join or key reconciliation, so two documents with the same `_id` from different collections both appear in the output. → https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-mongodb-how-to-use-unionwith-to-combine-collections-in-mongodb-aggre/view *(secondary; consistent with C8's UNION ALL semantics in the primary source)*

**C15.** Starting in MongoDB 6.0, `$search` / `$searchMeta` may appear inside the `$unionWith` sub-pipeline, but *"must be the first stage inside the `$unionWith` pipeline."* → https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/unionWith/

**C19.** **Use-after-free.** Cloning a sub-pipeline for `$unionWith` shallow-copied `Expression` objects whose `_expCtx` raw pointer still referenced the destroyed original `ExpressionContext`. Triggered during sharded pipeline dispatch with *doubly-nested* `$unionWith`, via the `$lookup` (`_letVariables`) and `$graphLookup` (`_startWith`) copy constructors. Fixed in 7.0.31, 8.0.20, 8.2.6, 8.3.0-rc2 — i.e. this class of bug was still live in supported releases as of the 2026 patch line. → https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-119319

**C20.** **Misleading explain (a).** `explain("executionStats")` on a `$unionWith` pipeline dropped the sub-pipeline's `$match` filter, reporting an empty `parsedQuery` and a `COLLSCAN` winning plan even though execution statistics proved an index was used. Fixed in 4.4.2 / 4.7.0. → https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-49469

**C22.** **Misleading explain (c).** Stages *created by pipeline rewriting* — e.g. a `$match` pushed down into `[{$unionWith: "test"}, {$match: {_id: 1}}]` — were not shown in `executionStats`, hiding the resulting `_id` index scan. Fixed in 4.4.11, 5.0.4, 5.1.0-rc0. → https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-58888

**Operational consequence of C20–C22:** on any server older than 4.4.11 / 5.0.4, a `COLLSCAN` in `$unionWith` explain output is not evidence of a missing index. Diagnose from `totalKeysExamined` and the index statistics, not from the reported plan.

**C23.** **Parser/server inconsistency, unresolved.** The MQL AST treats `{ $unionWith: { coll: "foo", pipeline: null } }` as equivalent to omitting `pipeline`, but the server rejects null pipelines. Still open, no fix version. → https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-46923

**C24.** **Missing optimization.** A `$group` following a `$unionWith` is not duplicated into each union branch with a merging `$group` after the union, so pre-aggregation on each branch does not happen. Deduplicating a large union (the C8 workaround) therefore concentrates all work in a single post-union `$group`. → https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-48121

**C27.** Amazon DocumentDB does not support `$unionWith`; MongoDB's own compatibility page lists it among unsupported aggregation stages alongside `$facet`, `$graphLookup`, `$merge`, `$bucket`, and others. → https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/documentdb-support/

This report covers the origin, release history, and behavioural evolution of the single MongoDB aggregation stage `$unionWith`. It traces the stage from the 2016 community feature request, through the January–February 2020 server implementation tickets, to its GA in MongoDB 4.4 and the behaviour changes documented through MongoDB 8.0 and the current manual.

Out of scope, and deliberately not researched: sibling stages (`$lookup`, `$graphLookup`, `$documents`, `$merge`, `$out`), the aggregation framework as a whole, and the parent domain `mongodb-aggregation-stages-deep`. `$lookup` is cited only where an official `$lookup` page states a fact *about* `$unionWith` (the MongoDB 8.0 namespace-validation change is documented on both pages) or supplies the same-database contrast needed to judge a `$unionWith` claim.

1. A public feature request for SQL-style `UNION` in MongoDB was filed as **SERVER-23201, "provide union operator to union two collections (or more)"**, type *New Feature*, created **2016-03-17**, with 31 votes and 41 watchers. It was eventually closed with resolution **Duplicate** and links to the `$unionWith` implementation work. — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-23201

3. **SERVER-45529, "Implement and test invalid usage of $unionWith aggregation stage"** — closed, fix version **4.3.4**, resolved **2020-02-06** — *depends on* SERVER-45399 and is *depended on by* **SERVER-45712, "Remove flag guard for $unionWith"**. The feature was therefore developed behind a feature flag and un-gated in a later 4.3.x development build. — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-45529

5. `$unionWith` shipped to users in **MongoDB 4.4**. The archived 4.4 manual page carries the marker **"New in version 4.4"**. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v4.4/reference/operator/aggregation/unionWith.md

7. Independent pre-release code analysis by Percona, published **2020-06-11**, already described `$unionWith` as a new 4.4 aggregation stage: *"It's UNION, but for MongoDB."* The same post notes the stage takes its own sub-pipeline, which is what makes unions of pre-aggregated or pre-filtered result sets possible, and that `UNION DISTINCT` has no single-keyword form — a `$group` must follow the `$unionWith`. — https://www.percona.com/blog/2020/06/11/mongodb-4-4-coming-out-soon-what-does-the-code-tell-us/

8. Independent post-release coverage by Severalnines, published **2020-09-04** (author Onyancha Brian Henry), documents the same 4.4 syntax, including the simplified `{ $unionWith: "<collection>" }` form. — https://severalnines.com/blog/what-s-new-mongodb-44/

9. The stage's 4.4 definition is *"Performs a union of two collections. `$unionWith` combines pipeline results from two collections into a single result set. The stage outputs the combined result set (including duplicates) to the next stage."* — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v4.4/reference/operator/aggregation/unionWith.md

11. The documented SQL analogue is `UNION ALL`, not `UNION`: the manual gives `SELECT * FROM Collection1 WHERE ... UNION ALL SELECT * FROM Collection2 WHERE ...`. Deduplication is the caller's job, via a `$group` stage placed after `$unionWith`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v4.4/reference/operator/aggregation/unionWith.md

12. `coll` may name a **collection or a view**. Collation rules follow the top-level aggregation: an explicit `collation` on `db.collection.aggregate()` wins; otherwise a `$unionWith` collection's own collation is ignored, but a `$unionWith` **view's** collation must match the top-level collection/view or the operation errors. This rule is unchanged from 4.4 through the current manual. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v4.4/reference/operator/aggregation/unionWith.md — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/unionwith/

22. **`$unionWith` is same-database only.** Its specification has never contained a field for naming a database: from 4.4 to the current manual the stage document accepts exactly `coll` and `pipeline`, where `coll` is *"the collection or view"*. The companion `$lookup` page states its own scope explicitly — *"Performs a left outer join to a collection in the **same** database"* — and directs cross-collection combination to `$unionWith`, i.e. both stages share the single-database scope. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/unionwith/ — https://www.mongodb.com/doc

- **Third-party claims about where a `$unionWith` sub-pipeline executes in a sharded cluster** could not be corroborated. The *Practical MongoDB Aggregations* sharding guide, the most likely independent authority, does not mention `$unionWith` anywhere; it discusses only `$lookup` merger placement. No execution-locality claim is made in this report. — https://www.practical-mongodb-aggregations.com/guides/sharding.html

This report covers the `$unionWith` aggregation stage only: what it does, how it behaves operationally, its documented restrictions, its optimizer gaps, and how practitioners should evaluate it. Sibling stages (`$lookup`, `$facet`, `$merge`, `$documents`, `$search`) appear only where a documented rule about `$unionWith` references them. The parent domain and adjacent stages are out of scope.

**C1 — `$unionWith` is `UNION ALL`, not `UNION`: duplicates are preserved and output order is unspecified.** The manual states the stage "outputs the combined result set (including duplicates) to the next stage" and that "the order in which the combined result set documents are output is unspecified." The manual gives `SELECT * FROM Collection1 ... UNION ALL SELECT * FROM Collection2` as the SQL equivalent.

**C11 — `coll` names a collection in the current database only; there is no `db` field.** The documented syntax for `coll` accepts a bare collection/view name with no database qualifier, and the MongoDB Search cross-collection guidance describes the capability as searching "multiple collections in the same database." The sibling stage `$lookup` states the same-database rule explicitly ("Performs a left outer join to a collection in the *same* database"). Cross-database unions must be done in the application or via a federated/Data Federation endpoint. *Confidence: moderate* — see the Unresolve
